pages.description: Check your small business website free in about 20 seconds: speed, phones, Google basics, security and tap-to-call, with the top 3 fixes in plain English.
pages.title: Free website check for small businesses
pages.lede: Type in your website and see what a customer on a phone, and Google, see. You get a grade, the three fixes that matter most, and a plain-English reason for each. Free, no sign-up.

list: Secure connection: whether the site loads with the padlock (HTTPS) and forwards the old http:// address to it.
First response speed: how long the server takes to start answering. Google's guidance counts 0.8 seconds or less as good and over 1.8 seconds as poor.
Page size and load: how heavy the page's code is, compression, how many scripts it loads and whether images load lazily, which all matter on mobile data.
Set up for phones: whether the page tells phones to fit it to the screen, plus image descriptions and the page language.
Page title and description: what Google shows as your name and summary in search results.
Main heading, sitemap, canonical tag and whether anything (a noindex setting or robots.txt) blocks Google from listing the site.
One-tap contact: whether a customer can tap your phone number to call you, and whether there's an enquiry form or email link.
Business details for Google: structured data with your name, address and hours.
Security basics: insecure files on a secure page and standard security headers.
Broken links: up to 10 links on the page, opened to see if they still work.
Share preview, visitor counting, a browser icon and whether the footer year makes the site look abandoned.

p: Each check is Good, Could be better or Needs fixing. The ones that cost you customers (no padlock, slow to respond, not set up for phones, hidden from Google, no tap-to-call) count for more. A is 90 or more out of 100, B is 75 or more, C is 60 or more, D is 45 or more. A low grade usually means a handful of quick fixes, not a rebuild.

sections.h: The fixes that usually matter most
list: Make your phone number a tap-to-call link at the top of every page.
Write a page title that says what you do and where, such as "Electrician in Bendigo | Your Name Electrical".
Add a 70 to 160 character description that gives people a reason to click.
Check nothing is telling Google to skip your site (a leftover "discourage search engines" setting is common).
Add your business details as structured data so Google can show your hours and address.

sections.h: What this check can't tell you
p: It looks at one page, the one you type in, plus a sample of its links, not your whole site. Speed is measured from our checker's server, so it shows how quickly your host answers rather than exactly what every visitor sees. It doesn't measure where you rank, your reviews or your Google Business Profile, which also decide how many local customers find you. Treat it as a quick health check, not a full audit.

faq.a: Yes. There's no sign-up. To stop misuse, each person can run up to 8 checks an hour. If you want help, you can send us your report, and that's optional.

faq.q: Do you keep the address I check?
faq.a: We save each report (the website address and its results) so you get a link you can share, for example with your web person. We don't save your name or email unless you send us the form. Your internet address is kept for a day, only to stop misuse. A repeat check of the same site within 30 minutes shows the saved report.

faq.q: Can I check a competitor's website?
faq.a: Yes. It works on any public website, which makes it a handy way to compare.

faq.q: Why is my speed different from Google PageSpeed Insights?
faq.a: PageSpeed loads the whole page in a test phone and scores everything, including images. We time the server's first response, the step every visitor waits for before anything appears. Both are useful; a slow first response usually means slow everywhere.

pages.seoTitle: Free Website Speed Test for Small Businesses | IMN Labs
pages.description: Test how fast your business website starts loading, in seconds and free. See your server response time, page size and what to fix first.
pages.title: Website speed test for small businesses
pages.lede: How long does your website make customers wait before anything appears? Type in your address to see your server's first response time and page size, plus the rest of the check, in about 20 seconds.

list: First response time: how long your server takes to start sending the page. It's the wait before anything appears, and every visitor sits through it.
Page size: how much code the page sends before images. Page builders often add hundreds of kilobytes that phones then have to download and read.
Whether the site is set up for phones, since a slow page on a small screen is where most visitors give up.

p: Google's web.dev guidance treats a first response of 0.8 seconds or less as good, and anything over 1.8 seconds as poor. We use the same lines: under 0.8 seconds is Good, up to 1.8 seconds Could be better, and slower than that Needs fixing.
For page size we call 300 KB of HTML or less Good and over 1 MB Needs fixing. Images are extra, so a heavy page plus large photos adds up quickly on mobile data.

list: Ask your host whether caching is switched on. It's often a single setting, and it can cut the first response a lot.
Cheap shared hosting is a common cause. Moving to faster hosting or a content delivery network usually fixes it.
Remove plugins, sliders and chat widgets you don't use. Each one adds code to every page.
Resize photos before uploading them. A phone photo straight off the camera can weigh more than the rest of the page.

sections.h: How this differs from other speed tests
p: Tools like Google PageSpeed Insights load the whole page in a test phone and score everything, including images and scripts, which is thorough but slower to read. Our test focuses on the first response and page weight, the parts a small business can usually fix with its host, and adds the other basics customers notice: the padlock, tap-to-call and Google listing details.

faq.q: Why does my speed change each time I test?
faq.a: Servers answer faster or slower depending on how busy they are and how far away the request comes from. Results are held for an hour, so test again later for a fresh reading.

faq.q: Is this the same as Google's Core Web Vitals?
faq.a: No. Core Web Vitals measure what real visitors experience over time. Our test is a quick snapshot of how fast your server starts answering, which feeds into those numbers.

faq.q: Does a fast site help on Google?
faq.a: Google says page experience is one of many things it considers. A fast site mostly helps the people who visit it: fewer of them give up before the page opens.

pages.seoTitle: Free SEO Checker for Small Business Websites | IMN Labs
pages.description: Free SEO check for local business websites: page title, Google description, business details, sitemap and anything blocking Google, in plain English.
pages.title: SEO checker for small business websites
pages.lede: Is your website giving Google what it needs to show you to local customers? Type in your address and see your page title, description, business details and anything that blocks Google, with plain-English fixes.

list: Page title: the blue headline Google shows for your page. About 30 to 60 characters saying what you do and where works best.
Meta description: the short summary under that headline. Without one, Google picks a random bit of text from your page.
One clear main heading, so people and Google can see straight away what the page is about.
Nothing telling Google to skip the page. A leftover "discourage search engines" setting from when the site was built is a common reason a business can't be found.
A sitemap at /sitemap.xml, which helps Google find new and updated pages.
Business details as structured data (LocalBusiness), which Google can use to show your address, phone and opening hours.

sections.h: What this SEO check doesn't cover
p: Real SEO for a local business is also about your Google Business Profile, reviews, other sites linking to you and having a page for each service and area you cover. Those live outside your homepage's code, so a one-page check can't see them. Think of this as the technical starting line: if these basics are missing, nothing else works as well.

list: Put your service and your area in the page title, for example "Mobile Mechanic in Frankston | Your Business Name".
Write a description that answers "why you": years in business, areas covered, same-day service, free quotes.
Make your phone number tap-to-call and match it exactly to your Google Business Profile.
Give each main service its own page with its own title and description, rather than listing everything on one page.

faq.q: Will fixing these get me to the top of Google?
faq.a: Nobody can promise rankings. These fixes remove the technical reasons Google might skip or misread your site, so your other efforts, like reviews and a complete Google Business Profile, count for more.

faq.q: Can I check a competitor's SEO?
faq.a: Yes. Type in their address to see how their basics compare with yours.

faq.q: Do you need access to my website?
faq.a: No. We only read the public page, the same as any visitor or search engine.
